security.title: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass

  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (declared at packages.config:14; vulnerable range: >= 5.0.0, < 5.1.3)
    Recommended fix: upgrade to 5.1.3

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Edit binds TeachingMaterialImagePath from the POST request (line 130), maps the client-supplied path without containment validation (line 172), then deletes the mapped file (line 175). A crafted traversal path can resolve outside the intended TeachingMaterials directory and cause deletion of an unintended file.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: The client-controlled TeachingMaterialImagePath in CoursesController.Edit is passed to Server.MapPath and then System.IO.File.Delete with no canonical-path containment check. Relative '..' segments can escape the intended upload directory and direct deletion at another mapped file.

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Edit binds TeachingMaterialImagePath from the request, resolves this client-provided identifier with Server.MapPath, and deletes the mapped file. The input is not constrained to the intended upload resource, so a crafted identifier can select a file resource outside the intended scope.
